sources.claim: UK Home Office country policy and information note on sexual orientation and gender identity for Russia (June 2025) is the national framework this division is scored against: consensual same-sex activity is not criminalised, but same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned; the Supreme Court designated the international LGBT+ movement an 'extremist' organisation in November 2023; between 2022 and 2024 at least 139 individuals were affected by anti-LGBT+ law enforcement, with 'gay propaganda' fines up to 400,000 rubles (about £3,600) or 15 days' detention for individuals, and trans-specific healthcare was effectively banned in 2023. The note contains no division-specific information beyond that national framework.

Human Rights Watch (30 June 2025), the article's one Sakha-relevant datapoint: in November 2024 a court in Yakutsk imposed an additional sentence on a prisoner for allegedly showing the rainbow flag to other prisoners. Nationally, Russian courts have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions since the Supreme Court's November 2023 designation (defendants face up to 12 years in prison), and HRW documented 81 people in 98 cases found guilty since January 2024 of article 20.3 administrative offences for banned symbols, mostly on social media — the enforcement baseline this division's national-score assessment rests on.

The attached sources are national-level rather than regional: a country-organisation overview of the national legal picture, a June 2025 report on the killing of an 18-year-old trans woman in a different province (Cagayan), and a national news item on a case in another region (Batangas) that could not be retrieved at fetch time.

sources.claim: Outright International's Philippines country overview (updated 12 March 2026): same-sex conduct legal nationwide; no legal gender recognition (still required: no LGR pathway); Executive Order 100 s.2019 (signed 17 Dec 2019) created a Diversity and Inclusion Program, amended by EO 51 s.2023 to add a special LGBTQIA+ affairs committee, neither implemented as of 2025; anti-discrimination ordinances exist at barangay, city, municipal and provincial levels but national legislation filed since 1999 has not been enacted; a 2018 Social Weather Stations survey found 22% support for same-sex civil unions and a majority opposed trans women's access to women's toilets.

Alternative-media report (26 June 2025): an 18-year-old trans woman, Kierra Apostol, was found dead with signs of physical assault in a river in Peñablanca, Cagayan province on 23 June 2025 after being missing since 22 June; her mother reported the disappearance to local police; Bahaghari (national LGBT alliance) chairperson called the killing part of a pattern of violence against Filipino trans women and renewed calls for the SOGIESC Equality Bill. Case is in Cagayan Valley region, not Northern Mindanao — national-climate evidence.

Wikipedia's LGBTQ rights in the Philippines page frames what a visitor to Northern Mindanao stands under: no general national anti-discrimination law (only piecemeal local ordinances), transgender people may not change their legal gender, same-sex marriage is not recognized (the Family Code confines marriage to 'a man and a woman'), and the SOGIE Equality Bill remains pending in Congress. Citing MindaNews (24 June 2019), the page notes that only 4 local government units across all of Mindanao had passed pro-LGBT ordinances by mid-2019, consistent with the record's caution that the absence of a Northern Mindanao regional signal reflects sparse documentation rather than confirmed absence of divergence (including in Lanao del Norte, where the record notes adjacent Muslim personal-law courts operate).

visible.summary:
This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which found no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement signal: its 2024 share of national LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases was 0.48% (Movilh regional table). Its recorded case trend follows the national one, which rose in 2025 to a record; a low share is not evidence of safety — most regions outside the two biggest rose that year.

There is no region-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for this division; its recorded profile comes from the shared national case table. National frame: 2025 produced a record 3,620 discrimination cases on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression (+27.1%; 23% of all cases in 24 years), and 2024 was the first regression since the return of democracy. Protective national framework (Gender Identity Law 21.120 in force 2019, same-sex marriage 2022, anti-discrimination law 21.220) sits against concrete 2025-26 rollback (PAIG excluded from the 2026 budget; health-ministry circular N8 restricting PAIG for minors; legislative initiative CEI-57) and administrative document friction from Registro Civil identification-system issuance failures (Comptroller Final Report 264/2025), which is directly relevant to a traveller whose documents must match presentation.
visible.tangentialFactors: National frame applies: Movilh records LGBTIQ+ discrimination cases rising in this region during 2025 alongside the national increase; a recorded-case rise is adjacent to trans risk via general hostility but is not a visitor-specific exposure.
visible.localsOnly: Resident-facing: Gender Identity Law 21.120 name/sex rectification (12,669 people by Dec 2025; only 15.7% of adults who declared trans/non-binary in the 2024 census; the nonbinary X marker still requires a judicial process) and the PAIG gender-identity support programme removed from the 2026 budget affect residents, not visitors.

sources.claim: Chile country dossier (Outright International, published March 12, 2026) contains no Aysen-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding, which is the basis for this record's national-score assessment: same-sex marriage and adoption legal since March 2022; the hate-crime law has covered sexual orientation and gender identity since 2012; legal gender recognition by self-determination since 2019; a third sex option on birth certificates since 2006; and the 2025-26 rollback in which the Chilean congress excluded the Gender Identity Support Program (PAIG) from the 2026 budget bill, an action condemned by civil society groups and the national ombuds for children. The dossier itself carries no division-specific information.

Movilh's XXIV annual report (HECHOS 2025, published March 2026) supplies this record's division-specific figures from its national regional table: Aysen is placed at 0.65% of nationally documented abuse cases, with a +25% year-on-year rise, a share-based reading that the report warns reflects weaker local safety rather than low risk. Nationally, the report records a record 3,620 cases and complaints of discrimination in 2025 (+27.1%, the highest in 24 years), with only Valparaiso (-17.56%) and Metropolitana (-14.35%) falling while the other 14 regions rose; it reads the shift as hatred expanding into regions with less public debate, which is what this record's mid-share reading rests on. The 2024 share cited in this record's comparison is not reproduced in this 2025 edition.
